```
$ PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m pytest scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_f004_role_assignment.py -q
```

I addressed the sole i0 finding (**medium, correctness — unsafe dashboard mutation commands for project paths with spaces**). In `dashboard_projection()` the project `--project` argument was previously interpolated raw into the display command at `role_assignment.py:269` and `:282-284`, so a scope path like `/tmp/my repo` produced `dontpanic roles set implementer <executor> --project /tmp/my repo`, which parses as two tokens if copied/run. I applied both halves of the auditor's recommendation: the display string now shell-quotes the project argument via `shlex.quote(project_arg)`, so the path survives copy/paste as a single token; and I added a parallel `mutation_argv` field (with `global`/`project` argv arrays) carrying the raw, unquoted value so a UI can dispatch programmatically without re-parsing the string. I locked the fix with a new regression test, `test_dashboard_projection_project_path_with_spaces_is_safe`, which asserts the displayed command round-trips through `shlex.split` back to the exact expected argv (spaced path preserved as one token) and that `mutation_argv` carries the raw path verbatim. The existing no-secret-shapes test still passes since it already excludes path-bearing command templates from its scan.
